subject.title: [Bug]: restart storm from telegram.retry.jitter type mismatch + misleading doctor SecretRef for Telegram token

question: After the linked `retry.jitter` PR is resolved, should this umbrella issue continue tracking the SecretRef/CDP/multi-root service hardening branches, or should those be split into narrower issues?
rationale: The central crash-loop branch has an open candidate PR, but the remaining branches cross SecretRef diagnostics, service supervision, browser profile isolation, and multi-user host policy, which is a maintainer scoping decision rather than a safe automatic fix lane.

options.title: Resolve jitter first, then split leftovers
options.body: Keep this issue open until the linked jitter PR lands or closes, then split any confirmed SecretRef/CDP/multi-root gaps into smaller issues before closing the umbrella.

options.title: Split the umbrella now
options.body: Create narrower canonical issues immediately for SecretRef diagnostics and service/profile isolation while leaving the linked PR to own only boolean `retry.jitter`.

options.title: Treat jitter as the only blocker
options.body: Close this issue after the jitter repair lands even if the broader diagnostic and service-isolation observations remain only partially assessed.

recommendation.title: Resolve jitter first, then split leftovers
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the linked jitter PR lands or closes, then split any confirmed SecretRef/CDP/multi-root gaps into smaller issues before closing the umbrella.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision spans config compatibility, doctor migration boundaries, and service reliability policy, and history ties this owner to both retry policy and doctor migration architecture.
